title: A modification of the constant-head permeameter to measure saturated hydraulic conductivity of highly permeable media
author: Nijp, Metselaar, et al.

steps.title: Assemble top and sample rings
steps.instruction: Connect the top ring to the sample ring ensuring a water‑tight seal.

steps.title: Place filter cloth
steps.instruction: Lay a filter cloth (mesh ≈ 0.001 m) beneath the sample and secure it with an elastic around the sample ring to prevent the sample from falling out.

steps.title: Position sample on grid
steps.instruction: Place the sample on a non‑ferrous or plastic grid platform (mesh >0.005 m) and verify that the grid is horizontally level.

steps.title: Saturate sample from below
steps.instruction: Add water (matching field chemical composition) until the water level reaches the bottom of the sample; slowly saturate the sample from below to avoid air entrapment (saturation is rapid for highly permeable soils).

steps.title: Prepare reservoirs
steps.instruction: Fill the collection reservoir and add enough water to the overflow reservoir so it can be pumped and recycled to the top of the sample.

steps.title: Connect inlet tubing
steps.instruction: Attach tube (6) to the water inlet; allow water to enter the sample via the wall of the top PVC ring (not directly onto the sample) and start with low pumping rates until a water layer is established.

steps.title: Measure sample dimensions
steps.instruction: Measure the sample height (dz, the distance over which pressure difference is applied) and the sample cross‑sectional area (A).

steps.title: Determine hydraulic head
steps.instruction: Measure (i) the distance from the water level inside the top PVC ring to its rim (H2) and (ii) the distance from the water level outside the top PVC ring to the top of the PVC ring (H1); compute the head difference as H1 − H2.

substeps.instruction: Measure H2 distance (inside water level to rim)
Measure H1 distance (outside water level to top of ring)

steps.title: Collect outflow and time
steps.instruction: Place a ~2 L beaker or Erlenmeyer flask under the collection reservoir outlet, start timing, and record the elapsed time until the container is removed; repeat until three successive outflow times differ by less than 10 %, then calculate the logarithmic average to estimate hydraulic conductivity.

substeps.instruction: Record time when container is removed
Repeat until three measurements within 10 % variance
Compute logarithmic average of the three measurements
